statements.text: 0, 1 and 2 are called the set of zeroes of the function.

If $f : \mathbb{R} \longrightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is a polynomial in x, then the set of values of x which makes $f(x)=0$ is called the set of zeroes of the function f and is denoted by the symbol $Z(f)$. Formula: $Z(f)=\{x: f(x)=0\}$

context.text: Imagine a school club sells small notebooks. Its profit in pounds from selling $x$ notebooks is $f(x)=x^2-5x+6$ ... Suppose instead the club checks $x=1$, $x=2$ and $x=3$ notebooks. Work out $f(1)$, $f(2)$ and $f(3)$. Which of these values of $x$ make the profit exactly $0$, and so belong to the set $Z(f)$?

statements.text: Z(f) is the solution set of the equation f(x) = 0.
To get the zeros of the function f, put f(x) = 0 and solve the resulting equation to find the set of values of x.

context.text: Imagine a phone plan where your balance in pounds after $x$ days is $f(x)=60-4x$. The balance reaches zero on the day when $f(x)=0$. Put $f(x)=0$ and solve the equation to find the set of zeroes $Z(f)$. What does that tell you about the day the balance runs out?
